title: Software Engineer Backend
description:
About Us
Our software solves the most critical emerging grid integration challenges to ensure that the impending energy transition is clean, equitable, and resilient. Our enterprise solutions help the grid absorb the coming electrification wave with ease. Utilizing modern, cloud-native platform architecture and robust systems optimization, WeaveGrid’s software is built from the ground up to tackle the most critical network challenges while meeting the stringent regulatory, security, and reliability requirements of the utility industry.
About the job
WeaveGrid's clean energy SaaS products monitor and manage a growing portfolio of distributed energy resources, including electric vehicles and battery energy storage systems, on behalf of electric utilities. We are seeking a seasoned backend engineer to independently design, implement, and deploy software with our partner device manufacturers and utilities. In this role, you will contribute to the technical direction of the team and help raise the bar for engineering quality. The impact of your code will be broad, from deeply integrating with diverse device manufacturer APIs, to monitoring and understanding battery status, to scheduling and verifying optimal charge or discharge plans, to ingesting, aggregating, and integrating signals from various utility sources.
In this role, we will ask you to:

- Design and produce high quality code for robustness, testability, and maintainability

- Work with our Python backend, relational database schemas, and microservice architecture & develop deep ownership of your area of work, including its long-term health, reliability, and technical debt

- Partner closely with Product Managers and business stakeholders to design and deliver new, scalable product features that expand our platform’s Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) capabilities.

- Collaborate with engineers to improve system reliability, data quality, effectiveness, and scalability across our product and codebase.

- Perform rollouts, instrumentation, alerting, and reliability monitoring in our production cloud environment

- Create brand new capabilities with new partners while reusing and generalizing existing modules

- Use Docker containers, Kubernetes, AWS, GitHub, Jira/Confluence, and CircleCI

- Participate in on-call rotations, periodically (~once per quarter) serving as the frontline presence for monitoring, diagnosing, and triaging production service issues

- Coordinate with multiple teams across several codebases in the engineering organization

- Contribute to team prioritization by identifying and proposing improvements to your area of work, including new capabilities, reliability investments, and technical debt reduction

- Special projects and other duties as designated by your manager or assigned designee

About you

- You are driven to use your skills and talents to help fix the climate crisis

- Preferred : you have a Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or

- You have 3+ years of relevant engineering experience, with a demonstrated track record of delivering complex backend systems independently

- If working remotely, you are available during core collaboration hours — approximately 9am–2pm Pacific — with flexibility outside that window.

- If you’re based in the San Francisco Bay Area, you will be working from our San Francisco office 2 days/week

- You care about the craft of software and feel a sense of ownership about code

- You leverage AI tools effectively in your workflow, including for coding, while maintaining the engineering judgment to critically evaluate and catch AI-generated errors or subtle incorrectness

- You enjoy solving hard technical problems and are excited to tackle the complexity of software that interacts with the real world

- You think in systems, independently scoping and delivering end-to-end projects with an understanding of how your work fits into the broader architecture - and you proactively surface and resolve ambiguity rather than waiting for it to be clarified

- You are proficient in a language like Go or Python and have expertise building microservices in a cloud-based backend

- You enjoy being hands-on in the full lifecycle of software development: early design, testing, production deployment, post-launch iteration, measuring and monitoring outcomes, and quickly fixing problems that may arise

- You thrive in a fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous environment, where priorities frequently shift to meet changing business needs and you help others navigate that ambiguity effectively

The total compensation for this opportunity includes a base salary range of $116,000- 165,000 plus equity (stock options) and benefits. This is our target compensation range and is subject to multiple factors including role, level, experience, and location. Please note that WeaveGrid may not necessarily hire individuals at or near the top of the base salary range, which is usually reserved for San Francisco, New York City, and Seattle candidates. As you go through our interview process, our recruiter will work with you to identify a competitive base salary within the proposed range and combine it with an equity package to get you excited about your future at WeaveGrid.

title: Associate Director, Business Development & Strategic Partnerships
description:
About Us
Our software solves the most critical emerging grid integration challenges to ensure that the impending energy transition is clean, equitable, and resilient. Our enterprise solutions help the grid absorb the coming electrification wave with ease. Utilizing modern, cloud-native platform architecture and robust systems optimization, WeaveGrid’s software is built from the ground up to tackle the most critical network challenges while meeting the stringent regulatory, security, and reliability requirements of the utility industry.

About the Role
WeaveGrid is seeking an Associate Director, Business Development & Strategic Partnerships to develop new business with electric utilities and build partnerships with automakers, EV charging companies, battery providers, and other distributed energy companies.
Reporting to the VP of Market Development & Partnerships, this senior individual contributor will own a focused portfolio of high-priority utility and partner opportunities. You will identify and qualify opportunities, build relationships with senior decision-makers, develop compelling commercial and strategic value propositions, negotiate agreements, and help translate signed deals into successful launches and revenue.
This role is well suited for someone who combines the consultative approach and persistence required for enterprise utility sales with the creativity and ecosystem thinking required for strategic partnerships. You should be comfortable creating new relationships, navigating complex organizations, structuring deals with multiple stakeholders, and remaining involved long enough to ensure that agreements produce meaningful results.

In This Role, You Will Be Responsible For

Business Development

- Own a prioritized portfolio of utility accounts and opportunities, advancing them from initial engagement through scoping, proposal, negotiation, and contract signature.

- Develop new relationships with utility executives and leaders across transportation electrification, distribution, grid planning, demand-side management, innovation, and operations.

- Lead consultative discovery to understand customer priorities, regulatory context, operational constraints, procurement pathways, budgets, and decision-making processes.

- Develop and lead proposals, presentations, business cases, pricing strategies, bid defenses, and other materials required to win complex enterprise opportunities.

- Navigate formal procurements, regulatory processes, pilots, and other pathways.

Strategic Partnerships

- Source, qualify, and advance partnerships with automotive OEMs, EVSE manufacturers and network operators, battery and energy technology providers, aggregators, and other strategic ecosystem participants.

- Build relationships with partner executives and working teams across product, engineering, energy services, marketing, and strategy.

- Identify and prioritize opportunities to create shared value through technology integration, joint go-to-market efforts, utility program delivery, customer acquisition, or new revenue streams.

- Develop partnership structures that clearly define shared value, commercial terms, responsibilities, technical dependencies, and paths to market.

- Maintain ongoing ownership of priority partnerships after signature, working closely with Client Success, Product, and other internal teams to support successful launches, increase customer enrollment and participation, resolve partner-level barriers, identify expansion opportunities, and track partnership performance.

Cross-Functional Leadership

- Drive clear internal alignment on priorities, decisions, responsibilities, timelines, risks, and next steps across assigned accounts and partnerships.

- Shape compelling solutions and commercial approaches in partnership with Product, Client Success, Finance, and Policy, and Delivery teams.

- Coordinate effectively across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Policy, Finance, Legal, RevOps, and executive leadership.

- Develop concise decision memos, executive presentations, account plans, and recommendations that enable timely, well-informed decisions.

- Maintain strong operating discipline through accurate pipeline stages, forecasts, relationship maps, account plans, and CRM data.

- Translate customer, partner, and market insights into recommendations that inform product strategy, positioning, partnership priorities, and go-to-market planning.

About You

- You have 7–10 years of experience in enterprise business development, strategic partnerships, corporate development, consultative sales, or a related field.

- You have personally originated, structured, negotiated, and closed complex B2B opportunities, ideally with electric utilities, automotive companies, EV charging providers, energy technology companies, or similarly complex enterprises.

- You are a strong commercial thinker who can translate market dynamics, customer needs, financial analysis, regulatory context, and technical considerations into a credible business case.

- You bring sound judgment to long and ambiguous deal cycles, including where to invest time, how to navigate competing stakeholders, when to escalate, and when to walk away.

- You are comfortable operating independently in a fast-moving environment while remaining highly collaborative with colleagues.

Preferred Experience

- Experience with electric utilities, transportation electrification, distributed energy resources, or enterprise energy software.

- Professional fluency in one or more of the following areas: virtual power plants, DERMS, demand response, managed charging, vehicle-grid integration, energy storage, or grid planning.

- Experience negotiating agreements that include both commercial and technical components.

- Experience working with regulated customers or in markets shaped by public utility commissions and regulatory proceedings.

- Existing relationships across the North American utility, automotive, EV charging, and distributed energy resource ecosystem.

Location and Travel
This role may be performed remotely within the United States. Candidates should have convenient access to a major airport and be comfortable traveling periodically for customer meetings, partner engagements, conferences, and internal gatherings.

Compensation
The total compensation for this opportunity includes a base salary range of $135,200 - $169,000 plus equity in the form of stock options and benefits.
This is our target compensation range and is subject to multiple factors, including role scope, level, relevant experience, performance expectations, and location. Please note that WeaveGrid may not necessarily hire individuals at or near the top of the base salary range, which is usually reserved for San Francisco, New York City, and Seattle candidates. During the interview process, our recruiting team will work with candidates to identify a competitive compensation package within the applicable range and combine it with an equity package.

title: Manager, Policy and Regulatory Affairs
description:
About Us
Our software solves the most critical emerging grid integration challenges to ensure that the impending energy transition is clean, equitable, and resilient. Our enterprise solutions help the grid absorb the coming electrification wave with ease. Utilizing modern, cloud-native platform architecture and robust systems optimization, WeaveGrid’s software is built from the ground up to tackle the most critical network challenges while meeting the stringent regulatory, security, and reliability requirements of the utility industry.
About the role:
Electric utilities design major EV managed charging and virtual power plant (VPP) programs in line with legislative and regulatory directives and in consultation with their respective regulators. In this role, you will shape and execute our strategy to accelerate EV adoption and other flexible loads to deliver value for our utility customers.

This role will be focused on policy and regulatory strategy in one or more subsets/regions of the United States while working hand-in-hand with the business’s leaders to inform WeaveGrid’s strategy and sales priorities. Success in this role will enable a long-term, sustainable pathway for WeaveGrid’s growth. This role will report to the Director of Regulatory Affairs and Market Development and work closely with the business development and the utility solutions team members supporting the region(s).

- Develop and execute WeaveGrid’s policy and regulatory strategy for the assigned U.S. region(s)

- Build external alliances and recognize opportunities for the company to build key relationships across stakeholders

- Write and submit comments for utility regulatory proceedings

- Attend conferences, workshops, and other convenings as a representative of WeaveGrid

- Research key regulatory developments to inform business strategy with an outlook of 2-3 years, and conversely, find avenues to influence policy and rule-, and rate-making per the company’s long-term objectives

- Research detailed regulatory filings, state-level policies, and competitive landscapes to track and support market and business development

- Collaborate with other business units to support benefit-cost analysis and review program evaluation results and materials

- Collaborate with the business development team to support beneficial outcomes and secure regulatory approval

- Assist the business development team in creating high-quality presentation materials on policy outcomes for important utility-client meetings

- Identify and pursue opportunities for formal and informal influence in the industry and regulatory realm

About you:
First and foremost, you’re mission-driven and fully dedicated to driving solutions for our climate crisis. You know that’s no small order and have developed a strong feeling that electric utilities and automakers are essential partners to make this vision a reality.

You have a deep sense of the needs and hurdles faced by a wide range of stakeholders that engage with the policies and regulations that impact our electric grid’s current operations and priorities for modernization. You thrive on the nitty-gritty world of policy and regulatory affairs because you’ve seen how it ultimately shapes and creates real change in our markets.

You bring a process-driven approach to your work day-to-day and a well-organized communication style. You know how to translate key details in a complex policy, filing, or other proceedings into actionable recommendations for our team. You’ve enjoyed working in a fast-paced environment at a high-growth company that thrives on a collaborative attitude, both internally and externally.

- BA/BS, or equivalent experience, in law, social sciences, or engineering Preferred: MPA/Masters, JD, or equivalent experience, with focus on energy policy regulations

- 5+ years of full-time experience in directly relevant policy and regulatory affairs for electric utilities and/or grid operations

- Significant domain expertise through industry experience in one or several of the following areas: transportation electrification, managed charging, DER flexibility, power systems, RTOs/ISOs, grid modernization, distribution planning, public utility regulation

- Proven skill set for: in-depth analysis of energy policy, regulatory writing, and/or state legislative lobbying

- Existing network among stakeholders in electric transportation, demand-side management, and/or grid modernization is preferred

- Demonstrated track record of empathetic leadership, individual initiative, a spirit of inquiry, and solutions-orientation

- Aptitude to think, communicate, and execute strategically and tactically

- High attention to detail, strong interpersonal skills, and excellent work ethic

- Functions effectively under time pressure

- Excellent written and oral communication skills and ability to translate technical information into persuasive narratives

- Experience prioritizing among competing initiatives and evaluating the strategic value of new regulatory or stakeholder engagement opportunities

- Ability to work with diverse teams internally and externally and translate between various areas of expertise

- Propensity towards remote work with the ability to travel as needed

The total compensation for this opportunity includes a base salary range of $110,000 - $156,000 plus equity (stock options) and benefits. This is our target compensation range and is subject to multiple factors including role, level, experience, and location. As you go through our interview process, our recruiter will work with you to identify a competitive base salary within the proposed range and combine it with an equity package to get you excited about your future at WeaveGrid.
